272830179_9aea6d5d.text: The lateral hypothalamus is a major sensor of the body's energy status that is critical for the control of ingestive behavior and spontaneous physical activity. Orexins (orexin-A and orexin-B, OxA and OxB, respectively) are neuropeptides that are produced in the lateral hypothalamus and trigger many physiological processes. The major physiological role of the hypothalamic orexin neurons system was initially described as an important wakefulness-maintaining factor and a regulator of feeding behavior and appetite (Jacobson et al., 2022). However, studies performed in various peripheral organs have indicated that orexins have various regulatory roles (Kukkonen, 2016)(Couvineau et al., 2019)

272830179_84ac3425.text: .Orexins induce biological effects by interaction and activation of two G protein-coupled receptors, namely orexin receptor-1 and -2 (OX1R and OXR2, respectively)

272830179_8c954559.text: .Orexins modulate appetite, energy expenditure, and metabolism (Couvineau et al., 2021)

272830179_340b0bfd.text: .Orexin deficiency is associated with narcolepsy and is related to higher risk of developing obesity, as well as increased cardiovascular risk (Arvis et al., 2022)(Jennum et al., 2021). Transgenic mice that have ablated orexin-containing neurons acquire narcolepsy and obesity (Hara et al., 2005). A lack of orexins reduces physical activity and, consequently, decreases energy expenditure and increases adiposity. Conversely, exogenous orexins attenuate adiposity in rats and mice ingesting an HFD (Funato et al., 2009).
